item.title: Quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, the bhikkhu enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by thought and examination,…
item.description:
Quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, the bhikkhu enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by thought and examination, with rapture and ease born of seclusion. He drenches, saturates, fills, and suffuses his body with the rapture and ease born of seclusion, so that no part of his entire body is not suffused with that rapture and ease born of seclusion.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 2 – Sāmaññaphalasutta

item.title: The life of humans in this world is not known, Without sign, full of trouble, brief, bound to suffering. There is no effort by which…
item.description:
The life of humans in this world is not known,
Without sign, full of trouble, brief, bound to suffering.

There is no effort by which one can escape death.
After old age comes death — such is the nature of beings.

As ripe fruits are always in danger of falling,
So mortals, once born, are always in danger of death.

As a potter's clay vessels, large and small,
At last all break — so is the life of mortals.

From: Sutta Nipāta 3.8

item.title: And, friends, how is there fear of wrongdoing? Here, friends, a bhikkhu reflects: 'If evil, unwholesome states that have not arisen in me were to…
item.description:
And, friends, how is there fear of wrongdoing? Here, friends, a bhikkhu reflects: 'If evil, unwholesome states that have not arisen in me were to arise, that would lead to my harm' — thus he has fear. 'If evil, unwholesome states that have arisen in me are not abandoned, that would lead to my harm' — thus he has fear. 'If wholesome states that have not arisen in me do not arise, that would lead to my harm' — thus he has fear. 'If wholesome states that have arisen in me were to cease, that would lead to my harm' — thus he has fear. Thus, friends, is there fear of wrongdoing. Thus, friends, having ardor and fear of wrongdoing, one is capable of enlightenment, capable of Nibbāna, capable of attaining the supreme security from bondage.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 16.2

item.title: 'Contemplating the body as a body,' bhikkhus — concerning phenomena not heard before, there arose vision, knowledge, wisdom, and light. 'This contemplating the body as…
item.description:
'Contemplating the body as a body,' bhikkhus — concerning phenomena not heard before, there arose vision, knowledge, wisdom, and light. 'This contemplating the body as a body is to be developed' ... 'This contemplating the body as a body has been developed' — concerning phenomena not heard before, there arose vision, knowledge, wisdom, and light. 'Contemplating feelings as feelings' ... 'Contemplating mind as mind' ... 'Contemplating phenomena as phenomena,' bhikkhus — concerning phenomena not heard before, there arose vision, knowledge, wisdom, and light. 'This contemplating phenomena as phenomena is to be developed' ... 'This contemplating phenomena as phenomena has been developed' — concerning phenomena not heard before, there arose vision, knowledge, wisdom, and light.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 47.31

item.title: Bhikkhus, these four things are extremely far, far apart from each other. What four? The sky and the earth, bhikkhus, are the first thing extremely…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, these four things are extremely far, far apart from each other. What four? The sky and the earth, bhikkhus, are the first thing extremely far, far apart. The near shore and the far shore of the ocean, bhikkhus, are the second thing extremely far, far apart. The place where the sun rises and the place where the sun sets, bhikkhus, are the third thing extremely far, far apart. The Dhamma of an evil person and the Dhamma of a good person, bhikkhus, are the fourth thing extremely far, far apart.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.47

item.title: Thus he dwells contemplating the body as a body internally; or he dwells contemplating the body as a body externally; or he dwells contemplating the…
item.description:
Thus he dwells contemplating the body as a body internally; or he dwells contemplating the body as a body externally; or he dwells contemplating the body as a body both internally and externally. Or he dwells contemplating the nature of arising in the body; or he dwells contemplating the nature of passing away in the body; or he dwells contemplating the nature of both arising and passing away in the body. 'There is a body,' mindfulness is established in him to the extent necessary for knowledge and mindfulness. And he dwells independent, not clinging to anything in the world. Bhikkhus, that is how a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 22 – Mahāsatipaṭṭhānasutta

item.title: Brahmin, what do you think? Here, if a consecrated Khattiya king were to assemble a hundred people of various lineages and say: 'Come, those of…
item.description:
Brahmin, what do you think? Here, if a consecrated Khattiya king were to assemble a hundred people of various lineages and say: 'Come, those of you born in Khattiya families, in brahmin families, of royal birth — bring the upper part of a fire-making stick made of saka wood, sala wood, salala wood, sandalwood, or lotus wood, and turn it to produce fire and heat. And those of you born in low families, in hunter families, in bamboo-weaver families, in cart-maker families, in scavenger families — bring the upper part of a fire-making stick made of a dog-trough, a pig-trough, a laundry trough, or dry castor-oil wood, and turn it to produce fire and heat.' — Brahmin, what do you think? Does only the fire produced and the heat generated by those born in Khattiya families, brahmin families, of royal birth, have flame, color, and light, and can that fire be used for fire's purposes? And does the fire produced and the heat generated by those born in low families... have no flame, no color, no light, and cannot be used for fire's purposes?" — "No, Master Gotama. The fire produced and the heat generated by those born in Khattiya families, brahmin families, of royal birth — that fire has flame, color, and light, and can be used for fire's purposes. And the fire produced and the heat generated by those born in low families, hunter families, bamboo-weaver families, cart-maker families, scavenger families — that fire also has flame, color, and light, and can be used for fire's purposes. All fire has flame, color, and light, and all fire can be used for fire's purposes." — "So too, brahmin, if a person from a Khattiya family goes forth... he can attain the right path, the wholesome Dhamma. If a person from a brahmin family... from a vessa family... from a sudda family goes forth... he can attain the right path, the wholesome Dhamma.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 96 – Esukārīsutta

item.title: Standing to one side, the devata Candimasa spoke this verse before the Blessed One: They will go safely, Like deer in a mosquito-free zone, Having…
item.description:
Standing to one side, the devata Candimasa spoke this verse before the Blessed One:

They will go safely,
Like deer in a mosquito-free zone,
Having attained jhāna,
One-pointed, mindful, aware,
They will reach the far shore,
Like fish breaking a net,
Having attained jhāna,
Self-controlled, beyond faults.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.11

item.title: - When the mind is sluggish, bhikkhus, that is not the time to cultivate the tranquility enlightenment factor, not the time to cultivate the concentration…
item.description:
- When the mind is sluggish, bhikkhus, that is not the time to cultivate the tranquility enlightenment factor, not the time to cultivate the concentration enlightenment factor, not the time to cultivate the equanimity enlightenment factor. Why is that? Because when the mind is sluggish, bhikkhus, it is hard to arouse the mind with these things. Just as, bhikkhus, a person who wants to kindle a small fire, if he throws wet grass, wet cow-dung, and wet wood onto it, exposes it to rain and wind, and scatters dust on it, could he kindle that small fire?" - "No, Venerable Sir." - "So too, bhikkhus, when the mind is sluggish, that is not the time to cultivate the tranquility enlightenment factor, not the time to cultivate the concentration enlightenment factor, not the time to cultivate the equanimity enlightenment factor. Why is that? Because when the mind is sluggish, it is hard to arouse the mind with these things.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 46.53

item.title: Bhikkhus, then Prince Vipassī asked the renunciant: 'Venerable sir, what have you done, that your head is not like others' heads, and your robe is…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, then Prince Vipassī asked the renunciant: 'Venerable sir, what have you done, that your head is not like others' heads, and your robe is not like others' robes?' 'Your Highness, I am a renunciant.' 'Venerable sir, what is meant by a renunciant?' 'Your Highness, I am called a renunciant because I live well the holy life, live well the pure life, do good deeds, do meritorious deeds, refrain from harming living beings, have loving-kindness towards living beings.' 'Venerable sir, excellent is your renunciation, excellent is the well-lived holy life, the well-lived pure life, the doing of good deeds, the doing of meritorious deeds, the refraining from harming living beings, the having of loving-kindness towards living beings.'

From: Dīgha Nikāya 14 – Mahāpadānasutta
